headline: GOLD HITS $4,750, SILVER CLEARS $79: Metals surge as White House nears Iran ceasefire
snippet: Spot gold jumped 1.2% to $4,750 an ounce Thursday as reports of a near-finalized U.S.-Iran ceasefire deal sent the dollar lower and oil tumbling. Silver surged past $79, adding 3% on the session, with analysts saying precious metals could resume their historic rally 'as the fog of war lifts.'

headline: APPLE + PENTAGON OWN A PIECE: MP Materials up 30% as rare earth deals reshape the supply chain
snippet: MP Materials has gained 30% in a month as investors digest two landmark deals: Apple's $500M four-year supply contract and the Pentagon taking a 15% equity stake with a guaranteed $110/kg NdPr price floor. The Mountain Pass mine is America's only large-scale rare earth operation; its Texas magnet plant is targeting first production in 2027.

headline: AUSTRALIA'S BIGGEST 2026 GOLD DEAL: Regis Resources + Vault Minerals merge in A$10.7B transaction
snippet: In an all-scrip deal announced May 5, Regis Resources agreed to acquire Vault Minerals to create a A$10.7 billion (US$7.7B) gold producer with more than 700,000 ounces of annual output — leapfrogging Evolution Mining to become Australia's third-largest gold company by market cap. The deal is expected to close August–September 2026.

headline: SSR MINING EPS TRIPLES: Q1 blowout as gold margins surge, $1.5B Çöpler sale on the way
snippet: SSR Mining posted Q1 EPS of $1.15, crushing the $0.87 consensus estimate, on 84% revenue growth to $581.78M. Free cash flow hit $211M, pushing cash to $634M. The company simultaneously announced a $1.5B sale of its Çöpler mine stake — a clean exit from a troubled asset that simplifies the portfolio heading into a back-half production ramp.

headline: RECORD QUARTER: Torex Gold posts $539M Q1 revenue as Media Luna hits design throughput 9 months early
snippet: Torex Gold delivered record Q1 revenue of $539M, adjusted EBITDA of $359M, and $157M in free cash flow despite $165M in tax and royalty payments. The headline: Media Luna achieved its designed 7,500 tpd throughput a full nine months ahead of the technical report schedule, removing the last major execution risk from the company's flagship mine.

headline: OKO GOES DEEPER: G2 Goldfields drills 84.5m at 3.0 g/t gold at 1km — deposit still open
snippet: G2 Goldfields extended its high-grade OKO deposit in Guyana to a kilometre of depth with hole GDD277B returning 84.5m at 3.0 g/t gold from 915m — pushing mineralization 140m deeper. The resource stands at 1.6 Moz Indicated at 3.24 g/t plus 1.9 Moz Inferred at 3.31 g/t. G Mining Ventures is buying G2 in a C$3B transaction expected to close Q2.

headline: COPPER HOLDS $6/LB: Iran peace lift metals complex as Chile refining faces acid supply crunch
snippet: Copper futures held above $6 per pound for a second consecutive session Wednesday, rising to $6.14/lb on U.S.-Iran ceasefire optimism. A structural supply concern adds urgency: Middle East disruptions have cut sulfur flows to China, prompting Beijing to restrict sulphuric acid exports — a critical input for roughly half of Chile's copper refining capacity.

headline: LITHIUM TURNS: Morgan Stanley sees 80,000-tonne deficit in 2026 as battery storage demand surges
snippet: An energy storage boom — fuelled by China's power sector reforms — is pulling lithium from a 61,000-tonne surplus in 2025 to a potential 80,000-tonne deficit in 2026, according to Morgan Stanley. UBS is more conservative at 22,000 tonnes, but both projections mark a significant inflection for a metal that has been under water for two years.

headline: NdPr CORRECTS 21%: Rare earth prices pull back in April but remain 88% above January
snippet: NdPr oxide fell 21% in April to $99.61/kg — the sharpest monthly retreat since the Q1 rally — dragging neodymium and praseodymium oxides to roughly $109/kg each. Despite the pullback, prices remain 88% above their January open and well above the cost base for MP Materials and Lynas. China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement, due in June, is the key catalyst to watch.

headline: MINERS FINALLY MOVE: GDX surges 6.16%, SIL ETF 6.56% as gold stocks break months-long resistance
snippet: Gold miners broke above the $42–$46 resistance zone with a 6.16% session surge in GDX, while silver miner ETF SIL rallied 6.56% through the $38–$43 band. GoldSeek argues that miners have lagged the metal badly for months — and this breakout, if it holds, could signal the start of the catch-up trade retail investors have been waiting for.

headline: $21.6 BILLION IN Q1: Mining M&A hits strongest start since 2023 with 121 global transactions
snippet: Global mining deal value reached $21.6 billion across 121 transactions in Q1 2026, a 34% jump in aggregate value from Q1 2025, per White & Case data. The surge reflects rising commodity prices and supply-chain urgency. Full-year 2025 totalled $93.7 billion — the highest in 13 years — and 2026 is tracking to match or exceed it.

headline: WHO'S WINNING THE EXPLORATION RACE? Junior miners compete as budgets hit four-year highs
snippet: As gold trades near $4,700 and exploration budgets reach four-year highs, African Mining Online surveys which junior miners are leading the discovery race. Digital targeting tools, ESG compliance, and satellite imagery are reshaping how small teams deploy capital — and which jurisdictions are pulling the most exploration investment in 2026.
